the HTL vertex function is a function of only the Mandelstam invariants, the temperature, and the gauge coupling, and that the HTLs of the n-point vertex functions in QED are O(g 4 ) and in QCD they are O(g 3 T 3 ).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HTL vertex function in thermal QCD is O(g 3 T 3 ) for n= 4, and O(g 3 ) for all other cases, n=2 and n=3.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RTF provides us with the most complete description for the HTLs at finite temperature and density, and that the HTLs satisfy the Ward-Takahashi identity in thermal QCD and QED.

the n-point vertex functions with odd numbers of retarded indices are identical to the ITF vertex functions, and the HTLs with odd numbers of internal retarded indices satisfy among them the QED-type WT identities, while those with even numbers are different from the ITF vertex function and exhibit the O(g 2T 3 ) HTLs, which also satisfy the WT identities among themselves.
the RTF is a useful and consistent formalism to study thermal field theory, and that the QED-type HTL vertex functions are the basic building blocks for the HTL resummations in thermal QCD.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the n-point vertex functions in the physical representation in thermal QCD and QED in the real time formalisms are not all equal to their imaginary time counterparts, and that the HTL resummation in real time thermal QED and QCD can be carried out in a consistent manner.

the n-point hard thermal loop vertex functions can be systematically classified into two groups according to their external retarded indices and that the HTL resummation of Dyson-Schwingers equations is consistent in both the ITF and the RTF, despite the fact that the HTL vertex function belonging to group b), which is characteristic of the RTFs, is O(g 3 T 3 ) and does not exist in the ITF.
the HTLs, which are the leading order in the hard thermal loop approximation, are gauge invariant in real time thermal QED/QCD.
